short_answer: The Jewish Sharp is a real seller in the sense that it has a working store, published prices, an X account opened in October 2020 and an Instagram account. It does not name an owner, a city or an address on any page we opened, and its only listed contact on the site is a Yahoo email address. Picks are delivered by email, outside the site, so a buyer has no account record of what was sent.

Whether the picks win is not something we could check. The seller posts monthly spreadsheets with records such as "28-4" and "24-4" and calls them "100% transparency", but these are its own documents. We found no third party log of every pick with the line and the time it was sent.

Prices are high for the category: a week costs $795.95 and most monthly packages cost $2,995 or more. The terms promise money back after 30 days only on a full price package, only if you took every pick, and only with bet slips, while the same page says refunds are not available for any reason. If you buy, keep every message and every ticket from day one.

guarantee: The terms page contradicts itself. It first says: "Once a purchase is completed, refunds are not available for any reason." It then says: "We offer a 30 day money back guarantee (when purchased with a full price package) If you are not up after taking every single pick for 30 days. Bets slips are required for proof." The About Us page adds that the team "never make false promises or guarantees."

Read the conditions closely. Only a full price package qualifies, so a discounted or promotional purchase likely does not. You must take every pick for 30 days and prove it with bet slips, so one missed play could void a claim. One day and one week packages cannot reach 30 days at all. We found no page that says how to file a claim, how fast money is returned, or whether "up" is measured in units or dollars. Betting losses are never covered.

Each package box on the homepage also repeats the same small print, "1 GAME DAY PLAY" and "Limit 1 per customer", even on monthly and season packages. Ask in writing what each package includes before paying.

claims_note: The spreadsheets cover the first half of a month, not whole months, and without logging in we could read only the headline records in the posts. A buyer cannot tell from them which plays went to which package, at what price, or whether every play sent by DM and email is included. Note also the arithmetic in one older post: "34-10 our last 34 plays" adds up to 44 plays, not 34.

The About Us page is written as an essay ("In this essay, I will outline why...") praising the team in the third person, and it mentions "sophisticated algorithms and models" without any detail. The "20+ years" claim cannot be checked; the X account dates from October 2020 and the site footer says 2021.

Many X posts from 2020 and 2021 offered a free pick only if a post reached a set number of likes and retweets, for example "If we receive at least 100 RT's and 200 Likes, we will release it!" That is a growth tactic, not evidence of skill.
record: Independently verifiable: nothing we could find. There is no full, time stamped log of every pick with the line, odds and send time on a third party site, no contest results run by a third party, and no regulator or court record. Picks go out by email and DM, and the store says they do not appear on the buyer's account page, so even buyers get no site record.

Seller marketing: monthly first half spreadsheets with records like 28-4 and 24-4, photos of winning tickets, and streak posts on X. These are made and chosen by the seller. Losing days appear in customer complaints (see below) but not in the posts we read.

CapperTek lists the site as a "Pro Featured Verified Service". CapperTek's own page describes verification as getting the service website verified to gain exposure and traffic and to sell picks in its directory. It is not an audit of results.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no The Jewish Sharp account is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how its picks perform.
our_data.context: For scale: the seller's spreadsheet headlines, such as 28-4, imply winning close to 88% of plays. On the Watchdog board on 7 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Customer evidence on The Jewish Sharp is split. Every review on CapperTek is glowing, while an old Reddit thread mixes praise with sharp complaints. None of it includes a full record, and we could not confirm who any reviewer is.

customers.text: CapperTek shows 8 reviews, all positive. They praise customer service and low juice around -110, and several say the writer is up every month. One from Feb 2025 says plays hit "right around 80%" over eight months; one from Sep 2022 says 2 losses in 18 picks. Three were posted within two days in Sep 2022 and make similar points. Reviews are anonymous and none includes a pick log.

customers.date: Shown as about 2 years old on 7 Nov 2026

BBB returned no results for the name. The Facebook page showed 51 followers and "Not yet rated (0 reviews)". Trustpilot blocked our check, and TheRX search did not return results we could read. We found no Covers or SBR thread.

conflicts: We saw no sportsbook affiliate links or promo codes on the site pages we opened. Some X posts carry sportsbook hashtags such as #FanDuel and #DraftKings, which are not referral links.
The seller has a featured, verified listing on CapperTek, which CapperTek sells as a way to gain exposure and sell picks. Treat the reviews there with that in mind.
Audience size differs widely by platform: about 1.3M Instagram followers, about 39,000 on X, and 51 on Facebook on 7 Nov 2026. Follower counts say nothing about results.
strengths: Prices for every package are posted on the site before you buy.
A single game ($34.95) or day pass ($39.95) lets a buyer test the service without a large fee.
The terms put a 30 day money back offer in writing, with stated conditions.
Many posts show the price taken, such as -110 or -125, which is more than many sellers show.
concerns: No full public record. Every number we saw is chosen and published by the seller.
The terms say no refunds for any reason and also offer a conditional money back guarantee, with no claim process described.
No named owner, address or company state on the site. Contact is a Yahoo email and social DMs.
Picks arrive by email and do not appear on the account page, so the buyer must keep their own proof.
Very high prices: $795.95 a week, $2,995 to $9,995 a month, and $19,995 for a hockey season.
Reddit users describe losing runs that do not appear in the seller's posts.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: It is a working pick seller with a store, posted prices and social accounts going back to 2020, and it delivers picks by email and DM. It names no owner or address, and we could not verify that its picks win, because there is no full third party record.
How much does The Jewish Sharp cost?
On 7 Nov 2026 the site listed a single game at $34.95, a day pass at $39.95, a week at $795.95, monthly packages from $2,995 to $9,995, and a hockey season at $19,995.
Does The Jewish Sharp have a verified record?

No. Its records are monthly first half spreadsheets and winning tickets it publishes itself, such as "RECORD: 28-4". CapperTek's Verified badge is a website listing feature, not an audit, and no Watchdog graded record is matched to it.
Is The Jewish Sharp worth it?

For the money you get plays by email or DM, often posted near -110, and a 30 day money back promise with strict conditions on full price packages. What is unproven is whether the picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of plays, and the same terms say refunds are not available.
